newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar soars to 122 yen in Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soars to 122 yen in Tokyo trade.

text.p: The dollar surged to 122 yen, its highest level since February 1993, in Tokyo trading on Wednesday.

Buying by banks after the dollar rallied in U.S. trading pushed the greenback as high as 122.05 yen before it slipped back slightly, traders said. The dollar has been surging on the relative strength of the U.S. economy and on signs that key nations will tolerate its new-found strength.

The dollar had finished at about 121 yen in the United States on Tuesday after surging to a peak of 121.77 yen during the day on evidence that the Group of Three nations -- the United States, Germany and Japan -- would not stand in the way of its growing robustness.
On Wednesday, a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official told Reuters Japan should keep close watch on currency moves because there were signs the trends could speed up.

"There are signs that recent currency movements may start accelerating," Kosuke Nakahira, a special adviser to the finance minister, said in an interview. He added that wild swings were not good for business as they could lead to a loss of confidence in a currency.
Japanese officials have repeatedly said that excessive shifts in foreign exchange rates were undesirable, but many analysts say Tokyo has few viable options to prop up the yen.
